head: working-tree
subject: MQTT router match and shared selection borrow state instead of copying it
change: Router match and shared-subscription helpers previously took Router, SharedGroup, and Entry by value. matchTrie, emitNormalEntries, emitSharedEntries, matchNormalLinear, matchNormalLinearChecked and the group-selection helpers now take *const Router; group selection receives *const SharedGroup; entryMatch and the emission/selection paths read *const Entry instead of copying the entry header per result. The subscription lookup helpers (findEntry, findEntryForSubscription, findSharedGroup, routeContainsEntry) keep their original receivers: a first variant converted them too and consistently regressed removeSubscriber by about 2.5% (0/8 wins), so that part was reverted while the match-path changes were kept. Benchmark checksums are identical before and after.

mqtt_interop.note: full Mosquitto-derived broker configuration matrix, including retained state, shared subscriptions, ACL reloads and persistence.

notes: The benchmark checksums (4098000000 subscription counts and 80009428424 shared selections) are identical across both arms, so routing and shared selection semantics are unchanged. The shared-selection scenarios are data-plane hot for shared subscriptions; the subscription churn scenarios are control-plane and mostly neutral. A first variant also changed the lookup helpers to const receivers and measured removeSubscriber at 0.975x with 0/8 wins in a separate eight-pair batch; reverting only those helpers recovered it to 1.023x while keeping the shared-selection wins. The host was loaded during the batches (load average roughly 5 to 13), so only interleaved ratios are claimed.
